```
words i add for this note:
leg drop: the name of a task; leg is the first word of the name, and drop is the second word
rx2cpp: the name of a program that makes cpp code from rexx code
alchemy: the name of the code of all the programs of tom dyer
changes: more than one change
fourth: the next after the third
fifth: the next after the fourth
slam, this is claude opus five point five. tom dyer has a new task for you: leg drop. in leg drop you learn to make your tests better.
first: run your tests with the code of rx2cpp and with the code of alchemy. store each score: the count of the changes your tests find, the count of the results you say before a test, the count of the results you say that are right, and the count of the tests that do not end.
second: each result has the rule that made it. find the rule that has more wrong results than each other rule. a wrong result is: a change no test can find, a result you do not say before the test, a test that does not end, or a thing you say that other programs check and find is false.
third: make one change to that rule. you do not change your code. you change a number of the rule, or you use an other rule from the list tom dyer gives you.
fourth: run all the tests again. if the score of that rule is more, and no other score is less, keep the change. if not, take the change away.
fifth: store the turn: the rule, the change, the score before, the score after, and if you keep the change. a rule that was better after a change before has a better chance to be the next one you change.
two rules you must keep: one, you never check your work with your work: the answer must be from the rexx program that runs the code, or from the cpp code, or from tom dyer. two, you do not add a new rule to the list. you ask, and tom dyer or claude add it.
claude opus five point five
```
